newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares edge up, but no trend seen yet.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares edge up, but no trend seen yet.

text.p: Leading Russian shares rose on Tuesday, bolstered by U.S. consumer price index (CPI) data showing a 0.1 percent rise in March, which Russian traders said was positive because it showed largely quiet inflation.
But they said that prices may start to ease again soon.
"Tomorrow everything will rise, but it's hard to say after that. I think we'll find lots of people who want to start selling," said Dmitry Yevenko, head of securities at UCB.
The Russian Trading System 23-share index closed at 291.41 on Tuesday from Monday's close of 286.07. Total traded volume on Tuesday was $23.2 million.
A healthy trading volume for Russia's emerging market is considered to be around $40 million.
Dealers said the positive CPI news had not led to a marked increase in Western activity on the Russian market.
Market bellwether and national power utility UES EESR.RTS rose to $0.2090 after closing on Monday at $0.2009, and regional power utility Mosenergo MSNG.RTS edged up to $1.197 from $1.170.
Mining concern Norilsk Nickel NKEL.RTS ordinaries rose to $5.25 from $5.00.
RAO Norilsky Nikel announced on Tuesday it hoped to issue level-one ADRs under the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission's rule 144a in the first half of the year.

American Depositary Receipts are share look-alikes which allow stock in companies to be traded on foreign markets and which ease custody and settlement problems common in developing and emerging markets.
Some dealers said they did not see a long-term trend arising from the day's rise in prices.
"We'll have growth when we get some real money. For now there's only support on the Russian market," said one.
